name: Stylized rider price and waiting-time simulator

reference.authors: Nicholas Buchholz, Laura Doval, Jakub Kastl, Filip Matejka, Tobias Salz
reference.title: Personalized Pricing and the Value of Time: Evidence From Auctioned Cab Rides
reference.relationship: Motivation for heterogeneous price and quoted waiting-time sensitivities only. This simulator is not a replication, does not use the paper's estimates, and does not claim to represent Liftago or Uber policy.

real_data_use: Only coarse median fare and completed-count scales from NYC panel rows timestamp < 2026-02-15 02:00 UTC. No validation or test outcomes, no real trajectories, and no estimated structural elasticities.
target: Hourly median realized fare among completed synthetic rides; missing when fewer than 10 completions, matching the public-data target eligibility rule.
timing: Start hour with last hour's queue, past observed potential arrivals, and current observable exogenous vehicle capacity.
Some pending requests abandon. Quote ETA from remaining queue and predictable demand; choose a rider price using only lagged requests or calendar plus lagged potential-arrival forecasts.
Realize new potential riders; heterogeneous riders accept/reject using quoted price and ETA plus pre-generated uniforms.
Serve FIFO up to exogenous capacity times matching efficiency. Earlier requests keep their original quoted prices.
Carry unmatched requests forward; use their locked fares for later completed-fare medians. Update demand state only for the next hour.
choice: Three latent preference types. Logistic utility intercept - alpha*(price/base_anchor-1) - beta*(quoted_eta-base_eta). All alpha and beta strictly positive; prices are common across types, not personalized.
driver_side: No driver payment control or pass-through assumption. Vehicle capacity follows exogenous seasonal availability, slow adjustment and shocks. Rider pricing does not automatically change driver capacity or pay.
controller: Illustrative flat, reactive, and anticipatory price rules with randomized smoothing, lag, gain and caps. Anticipatory uses calendar, announced events and previous observed potential-arrival counts, never latent AR states or realized future innovations. It is not a Chronos policy; internal session-arrival data would be required and are absent in TLC. No policy is optimized or presumed superior.
heldout_policy_illustrations: Four fixed independent seeds for low/high price sensitivity and short/persistent unannounced shocks. None is selected for a favorable result or used in forecasting-model training. Each world shares the exact exogenous path and choice uniforms across all three policies. Quoted ETA is a model proxy, not realized wait.
reporting_limits: Hourly queue approximation is for a forecasting demonstration, not minute-level dispatch optimization.
No causal inference about Uber, no Uber One membership mechanism, no competitor behavior, and no welfare or profit estimate.
Revenue means gross rider fares on completed rides before driver payments and operating costs.
Policy comparisons use the same exogenous paths and rider-choice uniforms. Differences are model-dependent, not empirical treatment effects.
A lower synthetic training loss is not evidence of improved real-world forecasting; real holdout evaluation remains necessary.
